title: Homotopy triangulation and quasi-isomorphism system for sheaf dg modules
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ commutative, and use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cohomology of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of associative unital graded $\mathcal O$-algebras with an $\mathcal O$-linear differential of degree one, $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A right dg $\mathcal A$-module is a graded sheaf with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$; left modules have $d(am)=d(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(m)$. Tensor products mean sheafifications of the balanced graded tensor products, with direct-sum total grading and $d(p\otimes n)=dp\otimes n+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dn$. A quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for right dg modules with chain maps modulo homotopies $f-g=d h+h d$, where $h$ is right graded linear of degree $-1$. Then $K(\mathcal A)$ is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], with shifts $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_M$, unchanged right graded action, and distinguished triangles those isomorphic to $M\xrightarrow f N\xrightarrow i C(f)\xrightarrow{-p}M[1]$. Here $C(f)^i=N^i\oplus M^{i+1}$, $d(n,m)=(dn+f(m),-dm)$, and $i,p$ are inclusion and projection. The class $W$ of quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ is a saturated multiplicative system compatible with this triangulation [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]; it has both calculi of fractions and two-out-of-three. The cohomology sheaves are functors on $K(\mathcal A)$, and $f\in W$ if and only if $C(f)$ is acyclic. No boundedness or graded-commutativity assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Form the dg category of the specified right modules. Its degree-$r$ Hom group consists of families of sheaf maps $u^j:M^j\to N^{j+r}$ satisfying $u(ma)=u(m)a$, with $\partial u=d_Nu-(-1)^ru d_M$. For $m\in M^j$, the two extra terms involving $d(a)$ in $\partial u(ma)$ have coefficients $(-1)^{j+r}$ and $-(-1)^{r+j}$ and cancel. Thus $\partial u$ is again graded linear. Expanding twice gives $\partial^2u=0$; expanding a composite gives $\partial(vu)=(\partial v)u+(-1)^{|v|}v\partial u$. Composition and identities are those of sheaf maps. Closed degree-zero maps are chain maps and degree-minus-one boundaries are exactly $dh+hd$, so $H^0$ of this dg category is the stated $K(\mathcal A)$. The zero module and degreewise binary sums give a dg zero object and dg biproducts: the coordinate maps are closed and satisfy the five biproduct identities. These operations need only finite sums of sheaves. Modules and maps in a fixed underlying universe form sets in a larger universe; apply the small-dg-category result there. This uses no small skeleton of the isomorphism classes of all modules.

For axiom (B), reindex by $M[k]^j=M^{j+k}$ and put $d_{M[k]}=(-1)^kd_M$, leaving the right action unchanged. The Leibniz identity is $(-1)^kd_M(ma)=(-1)^kd_M(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^{j+k}$. On a degree-$r$ homogeneous map put $u[k]=(-1)^{kr}u$, with reindexed components. The differential on simultaneous shifts is $(-1)^k\partial$, hence $\partial(u[k])=(-1)^{k(r+1)}\partial u=(\partial u)[k]$. Composition is preserved since $(-1)^{k(r+s)}=(-1)^{kr}(-1)^{ks}$; shifts compose by addition. Reindexing identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N[k])^r$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)^{r+k}$, and the differentials agree because $(-1)^kd_Nu-(-1)^ru d_M=(-1)^k(d_Nu-(-1)^{r+k}u d_M)$. For composition the first compatibility is the identity on components; the second has exactly the factor $(-1)^{k|g|}$ contributed by $g[k]$. These are the precise shift compatibilities in the cited ABC data. On closed degree-zero maps the shift has no additional sign.

source.place: Tag 0FRY section-shift-dg, correcting the homogeneous-map sign; Tag 0FS4

proof.text: For a chain map $f:M\to N$, form the displayed cone with componentwise right action. Its differential squares to zero since $d_Nf=fd_M$; its Leibniz identity follows in the first coordinate from that of $N$ and $f(ma)=f(m)a$, and in the second from the shifted-module identity of step 2. The sequence $N\xrightarrow i C(f)\xrightarrow p M[1]$ has graded splitting $s(m)=(0,m)$ and $\pi(n,m)=n$; its five splitting identities hold by the two coordinate projections. Its boundary is $\pi\partial s=\pi d_Cs=f$, representing $f[1]:M[1]\to N[1]$ under the target-shift Hom identification. This verifies axiom (C) with precisely the cone in the item, not an unspecified isomorphic cone.

Apply the generic ABC triangulation theorem to the dg category and the data verified in steps 1--3. Its closed maps modulo boundaries are exactly the specified chain maps modulo homotopy. It supplies the triangulated structure with the indicated shifts, and its last sentence identifies distinguished triangles precisely with those isomorphic to $(M,N,C(f),f,i,-p)$. Thus the sign of the third arrow is the required negative projection. No boundedness or commutativity of $\mathcal A$ entered any verification.

source.place: Tag 0FS7 proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated, invoking dga Tag 09QY and Tag 09QU

proof.text: Forget the $\mathcal A$-action. A dg homotopy is an underlying $\mathcal O$-linear chain homotopy, so this gives $U:K(\mathcal A)\to K(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O))$. Forgetting preserves the actual shifts, cone objects and all three cone arrows, hence carries every distinguished triangle to one in the ordinary homotopy category. The latter is triangulated and its localization $Q$ is exact by the cited ordinary-complex theorem. Therefore $QU$ is exact. Composing $QU$ with the derived cohomology functors gives the underlying cohomology sheaves by the definition of the derived category. They are functors, and the cited long-exact-cohomology result shows that $H^0$ on $K(\mathcal A)$ is homological. In particular $H^n(M)=H^0(M[n])$. Homotopic representatives induce the same maps; explicitly on a cycle $x$, $(f-g)x=d(hx)$, an equality that descends to cohomology sheaves without choosing global lifts of local cohomology classes.

Apply the homological-kernel detection leaf to this $H^0$. Its kernel is exactly the full subcategory $\mathrm{Ac}$ of modules whose underlying cohomology sheaves vanish in every degree; the leaf makes it replete and triangulated. It identifies its cone class with the morphisms for which every $H^0(f[n])=H^n(f)$ is invertible, exactly $W$. The existing cone-system theorem now gives identities, closure under composition, both calculi of fractions and compatibility with the triangulation. Its hypotheses hold because $K(\mathcal A)$ is triangulated by step 4 and $\mathrm{Ac}$ is full, replete, contains zero and is closed under shifts and triangles by the kernel leaf.

source.place: Tag 0FT4 lemma-qis; derived Tags 05R5 and 05RG (the equivalent homological-kernel route)

proof.text: For completeness the cone criterion holds for the specified cone: forgetting its triangle and applying derived cohomology gives the exact segment $H^n(M)\xrightarrow{H^n(f)}H^n(N)\to H^n(C(f))\to H^{n+1}(M)\xrightarrow{H^{n+1}(f)}H^{n+1}(N)$. If every $H^n(f)$ is invertible, exactness forces the middle object to vanish; conversely vanishing for all $n$ makes every $H^n(f)$ both monic and epic, hence invertible in the abelian category of sheaf modules. Two-out-of-three follows degreewise for isomorphisms. Saturation in the specified stronger sense follows as well: if $fg$ and $gh$ induce isomorphisms, then in each degree $H(g)$ has left inverse $H(fg)^{-1}H(f)$ and right inverse $H(h)H(gh)^{-1}$; these inverses coincide, so $g\in W$. Together with step 6 these are all clauses of the saturated compatible multiplicative system definition.
